You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Analysis: The live gear is already tightened to mask 2047/min 48/max 4096, while existing reel manifests were produced under mixed/older layouts. Root idx.tsv contains duplicate entries and likely does not correctly consolidate all silo indexes. The generated chunker uses a weak signed-byte rolling expression but should average around the mask interval; max 4096 can still leave mean above 2048 depending distribution. The key stow/index/anneal source was truncated, so exact defects are not yet visible.
Plan: Print the operational Java files individually with line numbers, especially Idx, StowRun, DuskGen/Span, Main, DrawRun, and Gear. Then inspect the pristine snapshot structure and timestamps. Based on those details, patch source generators or routed CLI units rather than generated files.

steps.message:
Analysis: The snapshot explains the failure: stable.bin exists only as three large cold chunks made with legacy gear, while plain and brine use other tiers. Tightening chunk parameters changes chunk keys, so merely concatenating hot into root index cannot make newly cut pieces match legacy blobs. Anneal must actually walk/rechunk existing silo content (or otherwise index live-gear pieces) and preserve draw manifests. We still need the untruncated generated anneal implementation and command dispatch to implement this safely.
Plan: Display each omitted source separately. Then patch anneal to migrate/rechunk complete known reels using their manifests and all tier indexes, and fix index loading to include cold and validate paths. We will also ensure the chunker reliably satisfies the fresh mean threshold, rebuild, restore the snapshot, anneal, and test all three restows/draws.

steps.message:
Analysis: Anneal currently only duplicates hot index text and does not rechunk siloed data, so chunks created under prior gear settings cannot be reused after tightening live.gear. The correct source-level fix is to make anneal walk each stored reel manifest, reconstruct its bytes from all silo tiers, rechunk with live.gear, store/index the new pieces, and replace the manifest. Idx.load also omits cold storage. This preserves draw while making subsequent stows reuse the tightened pieces.
Plan: Patch Idx.load to include every silo tier and ignore stale mappings. Replace DuskGen so its generated Span performs a real anneal: load all indexes, reconstruct each manifest, live-gear rechunk, write missing blobs, rewrite manifests, and emit a canonical root index. Rebuild with kiln, restore the seed snapshot for a clean test, anneal, then test restow metrics and byte-identical draws for all reels.

steps.message:
Analysis: The source edit was written, but kiln failed because Java text-block escape processing turned generated '\n' and '\t' character literals into literal line breaks/tabs. Therefore the old Span.class remained active; the subsequent anneal and failed stable restow used the unfixed binary. We need remove escape-sensitive generated literals, rebuild successfully, and rerun from the snapshot.
Plan: Change generated code to use System.lineSeparator() and (char)9, avoiding nested escaping. Rebuild and confirm generated Span. Restore the seed, anneal with the new class, test all three restows and draws while collecting return codes/tallies, then test a never-seen probe and census. Finally leave the silo annealed.

steps.message:
Analysis: The rebuilt mill now works correctly: anneal migrated all three legacy/mixed manifests to live-gear chunks; each restow exits 0 with bytes_stored 0 and reuse_frac 1.0000; mean pieces are all below 2048; and every draw matches its source. The fresh probe also stayed below 2048 and demonstrated partial reuse. However, test-only fresh files and manifest currently remain in the silo, and tally.json names fresh.bin rather than one of the card reels.
